PullRequest.Title: Titlebar owns compact menu when Activity Bar is hidden
PullRequest.Body:
Fixes #144216

## What

With `window.menuBarVisibility: "compact"` and the Activity Bar hidden (`workbench.activityBar.location: "hidden"`), the compact menu was not shown anywhere and Alt+F (and the other Alt+letter menu mnemonics) did nothing. The title bar now hosts the compact menu in that configuration, the same way it already does when the Activity Bar is at the top or bottom.

## Why

The compact menu lives in the Activity Bar unless `isCompactMenuInTitlebar` hands it to the title bar. #345401 added that handoff for the top and bottom positions, but `hidden` still left the menu in a part that is never shown, so the menu and its mnemonics were unreachable. In addition, `isTitleBarEmpty` only treats top/bottom as title bar content, so on web or in desktop fullscreen the title bar would hide itself even if it owned the menu.

## How

- `isCompactMenuInTitlebar` treats `hidden` like `top` and `bottom`. The existing install/uninstall, popup-direction and zoom logic in the title bar and Activity Bar already follow this predicate.
- `isTitleBarEmpty` now considers the main window title bar non-empty when the Activity Bar is hidden and the menu is compact, so the title bar stays visible to host the menu (web, desktop fullscreen). Auxiliary windows and other menu visibilities are unaffected; the existing fallback to the Activity Bar when the custom title bar is hidden (`customTitleBarVisibility: never`/`windowed`) is unchanged.
- Tests in `titlebarPart.test.ts` and `activitybarPart.test.ts` cover `hidden` for ownership, install/recreate, popup direction, creation, the custom-title-bar handoff, and the fullscreen title bar visibility (including classic/toggle and auxiliary windows staying unchanged).

## Evidence

- **Before** (Code OSS from `main`, compact menu + hidden Activity Bar): no menu button anywhere; Alt+F does nothing; in fullscreen the title bar disappears.
- **After**: the ☰ compact menu sits at the start of the title bar and Alt+F opens the File menu, including in fullscreen. Switching `default ↔ hidden ↔ top ↔ bottom` at runtime always leaves exactly one compact menu, owned by the Activity Bar for `default` and by the title bar otherwise.
- Unit tests: `scripts\test.bat --run src/vs/workbench/test/browser/parts/titlebar/titlebarPart.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/test/browser/parts/activitybar/activitybarPart.test.ts` → 55 passing, 1 pending (pre-existing skip); Chromium browser runner on the same files → 51 passing, 4 pending (handoff tests skip on web by design). Without the source change, 8 (Electron) / 6 (Chromium) of the new expectations fail. `pnpm run oxlint` on the changed files and `pnpm run typecheck-client` pass.

Full report with before/after screenshots, plan, reviews and verification: [engineer report](https://aka.ms/publish?a=73e1284c-8edc-4a0c-9587-12aeb0fb6090)

Note: while verifying, I found a pre-existing, unrelated issue: if the menu or Activity Bar setting changes from outside the window (for example another process writes `settings.json`) while a compact-menu submenu is open, disposing the menu bar throws in `SubmenuMenuActionViewItem.dispose` and leaves a stale menu bar. It reproduces with the Activity Bar-owned menu too, and does not happen when the setting is changed through the UI. Left for a follow-up.

Scenarios.Scenario: Workbench startup with `window.menuBarVisibility: compact` and the Activity Bar location set to `hidden`
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Initial layout evaluates title-bar visibility and menu ownership, then synchronously creates one `CustomMenubarControl` in the title bar. This work must complete before the compact menu is usable, but it is bounded to one control and one title-bar layout.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One main window and one compact menu; cost does not scale with files, editors, menu items at this ownership layer, or auxiliary-window count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single-threaded UI initialization; no queue, parallel fan-out, or concurrency burst is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache or miss path is involved. Configuration reads are direct service lookups; cold and warm behavior have the same bounded cardinality.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed predicate directly transfers ownership from the hidden Activity Bar to the title bar, and the title-bar visibility branch is directly reached during initial layout.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact DOM/layout duration varies by platform, but the diff relocates one existing menu control and makes one existing title-bar part visible rather than adding collection-scaled work.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The added synchronous UI work is constant and required to expose the menu; before the diff the existing control was owned by the hidden Activity Bar, while after it is owned by the title bar. No subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, network, or new serialization boundary is reached.

Scenarios.Scenario: Runtime changes among default, top, bottom, and hidden Activity Bar locations or custom-title-bar visibility modes
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A configuration event synchronously updates Activity Bar and title-bar menu ownership, disposes the prior menu control when ownership changes, creates the replacement, and performs a bounded relayout before the setting change is visually settled.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of relevant configuration transitions, with constant work per transition; no per-editor, per-file, or per-menu-entry boundary fan-out is added.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Configuration listeners execute on the UI thread; installation is guarded against duplicates and ownership remains one control at a time. There is no aggregate parallel work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is used. Each actual relevant configuration event performs one ownership check; repeated identical installation is suppressed by existing `menubar` guards.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: changed ownership for `hidden` reaches the existing install/uninstall paths in both parts, whose disposal and duplicate guards were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Menu creation and relayout cost are platform-dependent, but the trigger is an infrequent explicit setting change and cardinality is one menu per main window.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff adds a bounded ownership transfer when entering or leaving `hidden`, analogous to the existing top/bottom transfer, with explicit cleanup and no retained duplicate control or external expensive boundary.

Scenarios.Scenario: Entering or leaving fullscreen with a hidden Activity Bar and compact menu
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The fullscreen event updates layout state and synchronously calls `shouldShowCustomTitleBar`; the changed emptiness rule keeps the main-window title bar visible and the grid lays it out. The menu remains available on the same UI critical path.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One title-bar subtree per main window and one visibility evaluation per fullscreen transition; auxiliary windows are explicitly excluded.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One fullscreen event is processed synchronously for the main window. Activity Bar ownership checks and grid visibility updates are serialized on the UI thread.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache or coalescing layer is involved. The visibility calculation is constant-time configuration and window-state lookup for every fullscreen transition.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the added `isTitleBarEmpty` branch directly changes the fullscreen grid visibility decision for exactly the main-window compact/hidden configuration.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Keeping the title bar visible has a small persistent rendering/layout footprint whose exact cost is not measured, but it is one existing DOM subtree and does not grow with workspace size or event frequency beyond fullscreen transitions.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The constant rendering footprint is the intended host for the compact menu, and the diff introduces no repeated geometry read/write loop, frame-frequency work, external boundary, or unbounded allocation.

Scenarios.Scenario: Opening the compact menu by mouse or Alt mnemonic while the Activity Bar is hidden
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Input reaches the existing `CustomMenubarControl` now hosted in the title bar; popup direction is selected synchronously and the existing menu rendering path runs. No new prerequisite boundary is added by the diff.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One popup per user input; menu item count is unchanged from the pre-diff `CustomMenubarControl`.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One input event and one popup; existing menu interaction is serialized on the UI thread.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Ownership and popup-direction checks read current configuration directly. The diff does not alter menu-model caching, invalidation, or item enumeration.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the only changed production behavior on this path is the ownership predicate, while the popup implementation remains unchanged.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual menu size varies, but the diff does not change item cardinality or rendering behavior; it only changes which existing container owns the control.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Richer reachability of the existing menu does not increase its per-open work, boundary count, concurrency, or retained state.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all five changed files and traced startup, configuration handoff, fullscreen layout, and menu-input scenarios. The production change adds `hidden` to an existing constant-time ownership predicate and keeps one existing title-bar subtree visible when needed. Install/uninstall lifecycle remains bounded and guarded, and no subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, network, collection fan-out, unbounded retention, or hot-loop mechanism was introduced. No performance finding or regression-fix record is warranted.
